▸How it’s built — engine benchmarks, and the policy that trains inside ittap to expand
Simulation throughput

RoamingSim simulates a full metro network in 2.4 minutes — roughly 50,000× faster than microscopic SUMO. Fast enough to run the millions of rollouts the calibration engine needs.

Regime-aware orchestration engine

A compact spatio-temporal mixture-of-experts policy. Set to the owner-profit objective, it maximizes earnings while holding each owner’s hard availability constraint — with stable training and no reward hacking.

Working Platform · Demo
The day, narrated
One car, one full day
A private AV lives a working day in San Francisco while its owner is at work — out earning by 08:30, home charged before six. Everything on screen is the engine deciding, not an animation.
Offers arrive one at a time
Uber, Lyft, DoorDash. Each offer is a fifteen-second decision that reshapes the rest of the day — traffic, battery, and whether the car is where the owner needs it, when they need it.
Every verdict carries its reason
The journal logs each accept and reject in plain English — including declining the day's biggest fare because it risked the 6 p.m. return. Explainability is what lets an OEM put its brand behind this.
The fence is the promise
The shaded boundary on the map is “reachable by deadline” under live traffic. The car only earns inside the radius that still guarantees an on-time return.
Home, on time, every time
The day ends where it must: at HOME before the deadline, return SLA green, the day's net on the board. Reliability isn't bolted on — it's inside the objective.
Preference personalization
A week of trips in, a profile out
Import a real trip log and the platform classifies the owner into a behavior segment, then fits their personal utility Uw — the sliders animate to the result. Preferences are measured, not assumed.
Same day, different owners
Same city, same offers: a car-carer's policy declines what an earnings-maximizer takes. The radar shows RoamingOS hugging the owner's shape — not the platform's.
+32 points, scored by the owner
Scored by this owner's own utility, RoamingOS beats a platform-revenue policy 85 to 54 on weekly satisfaction — while still earning $394 for the week.
Why the pixels
The fitted weights are the product, so we redact them in shared decks. The live platform runs them end-to-end — ask for the walkthrough.
Availability personalization
A pipeline, not one clever model
Eight stages take an owner from raw trip logs to a served policy. The stages are our method — pixelated here on purpose; the outcomes around them are not.
Classified within a week
A new owner reaches segment confidence 0.83 in week one, and window uncertainty keeps narrowing as their own data accrues — the system learns one person's rhythm, fast.
A calibrated digital twin
The twin predicts when the owner will need the car: a population prior of ±88 min sharpens to ±18 min, with tail calibration an engineer can audit. That estimate is what moves the map's fence in real time.
This is the moat
Whoever learns an owner's rhythm fastest — and keeps up when it changes — wins the owner. This machinery compounds with every mile of real data.

Replay shown is calibrated-synthetic v0 on the real OSM Bay Area road network — the framework, routing, decisions and classification pipeline are real code; magnitudes are staged demo data and stay illustrative until offer-log calibration lands. Redacted panels run live in the full platform walkthrough.
